alignments.note: קֵהָה rendered *be blunt*; head on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 24, 44).
The explicit pronoun הוּא is realized by the impersonal *one*; it takes only its own English (rule 20).

CORRECTED: the negative takes only its own *not*. The accepted reading gave it *do not* whole on the analogy of rule 35's *cannot*, but that fusion holds only where the word is indivisible; rule 35's closing sentence splits a negation and an auxiliary written as two words, and rule 17's second limit rules that where no interrogative morpheme is present a fronted *do* is the verb's own (לֹא שָׁפָטוּ → *do they not judge*).
CORRECTED: the finite verb takes the do-support auxiliary along with its lexical verb (rule 17), discontinuous around the negative (rule 25); head on *whet* (rule 24).
פָּנִים rendered *the edge*; no article morpheme, so the supplied determiner joins the noun (rule 15).
Finite verb with its modal and subject pronoun; *to* is the English verb's phrasal particle, so the head stays on *put* (rules 17, 44).
The supplied quantifying determiner *more* joins the nominal expression it determines and is never the head (rule 15).
Nominal predicate with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
No preposition stands before the infinitive construct, so the English infinitive marker belongs to the infinitive's own unit (rule 52); head on the lexical verb (rule 24).

review_notes: Correction: *do not* split — *do* to the verb קִלְקַל, *not* to לֹא. Rule 35 fuses only an indivisible *cannot* onto the negative and splits a two-word negation-plus-auxiliary, and rule 17's second limit assigns a fronted *do* to the verb where no interrogative morpheme stands in the clause.
Variant WLC.ECC.10.10.v002 is underdetermined and resolved to r00-base; aligned as printed (rule 9).
